concept.name: In-Memory Caching & Event Loop Architecture
concept.tagline: Eliminate DB latency bottlenecks using single-threaded event loops, Epoll I/O multiplexing, and LRU/LFU memory eviction.

spark.summary: Caching stores high-frequency read data in fast RAM instead of slow disk/network databases. Redis achieves sub-millisecond QPS by operating a single-threaded event loop paired with OS epoll I/O multiplexing, completely eliminating thread locking contention.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use single-threaded I/O multiplexing for ultra-fast, lock-free key-value operations; guard against blocking O(N) calls and un-bounded memory growth.

concept.whyItMatters: Databases stall under concurrent read spikes. Placing an in-memory cache layer in front of PostgreSQL or Cassandra reduces p99 read latencies from 50ms to under 1ms, protecting disk I/O.
whenToUse: Session storage, rate-limiting counters, and leaderboards.
Expensive compute queries or third-party API response caching.
whenNotToUse: Datasets larger than available RAM without tiering.
Data with near-zero read reuse frequency.
keyPoints: Redis Single-Threaded Event Loop handles commands sequentially in CPU L1/L2 cache without thread context switching.
I/O Multiplexing (epoll/kqueue) allows one OS thread to monitor 10,000+ client TCP socket connections asynchronously.
Eviction policies (allkeys-lru, volatile-lru, volatile-ttl) automatically reclaim memory when maxmemory bounds are reached.

examples.title: API Gateway Rate-Limiting
examples.scenario: Scaling API gateway checking 50,000 requests/sec against user quotas.
examples.outcome: Redis INCR + EXPIRE executes atomically in <1ms without DB locks.

examples.title: Stripe Session Caching
examples.outcome: Cache-Aside pattern delivers 99.4% cache hit ratio, shielding auth DB.

tradeOffs.pro: Single thread avoids deadlocks, lock contention, and OS context switching overhead.
tradeOffs.con: Long-running O(N) operations (e.g. KEYS *) block all concurrent clients.

tradeOffs.pro: Cache-Aside handles cache failures gracefully by falling back to DB.
tradeOffs.con: Cache stale risk during DB updates requires strict invalidation or TTL.

failureModes.name: Cache Stampede (Thundering Herd)
failureModes.description: Hot cache key expires simultaneously under high traffic, causing 10,000 concurrent DB queries.
failureModes.mitigation: Use probabilistic early expiration (XFetch algorithm) or distributed lock mutex (SETNX).

failureModes.name: Single-Thread Blockage
failureModes.description: Executing KEYS * or large HGETALL halts the Redis event loop for seconds.
failureModes.mitigation: Use cursor-based SCAN / HSCAN instead of blocking full keyspace queries.

commonMistakes: Omitting Time-To-Live (TTL) on cached objects, leading to OOM crashes.
Storing large (>10MB) payloads that block network serialization.

deepDive.markdownContent:
## 📖 Core Mechanics: The Single-Threaded Event Loop & Epoll

Redis operates a non-blocking event loop wrapped in the `ae` system library. Instead of assigning a worker thread per socket connection (which causes CPU context switching and lock contention), Redis uses kernel-level **I/O Multiplexing** (`epoll` on Linux, `kqueue` on macOS).

```architecture
{
  "view": "high-level",
  "title": "Redis Event Loop & I/O Multiplexing",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "clients", "label": "10k Client TCP Sockets", "type": "client" },
    { "id": "epoll", "label": "OS Epoll Kernel Multiplexer", "type": "service" },
    { "id": "loop", "label": "Single-Threaded Event Loop", "type": "processor" },
    { "id": "ram", "label": "In-Memory Data Store", "type": "database" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "clients", "to": "epoll", "label": "Network Bytes" },
    { "from": "epoll", "to": "loop", "label": "Active Sockets Queue" },
    { "from": "loop", "to": "ram", "label": "Atomic Execute & Write" }
  ]
}
```

### ⚙️ Memory Layouts: Ziplists vs Hashtables
Every object is stored in a `robj` memory structure. For small collections (under 512 items or 64 bytes/item), Redis uses **Ziplists**—contiguous byte arrays that avoid 24-byte pointer overhead per node.

questions.title: Single-Thread Execution Bottleneck
questions.prompt: Why does Redis execute single-threaded command processing faster than traditional multi-threaded locked data structures?

options.text: It bypasses CPU RAM and reads directly from NVMe disks.
options.explanation: Redis is an in-memory data store operating in RAM.

options.text: It eliminates CPU lock contention, thread context switching overhead, and lock queues while using OS epoll I/O multiplexing.
options.explanation: Correct! Running commands sequentially on a single thread avoids thread locking overhead.

rubric.excellent: Identifies lock contention, CPU context switching reduction, and epoll multiplexing.
rubric.gap: Confuses disk storage with in-memory operation.

questions.sampleSolution: Redis avoids thread synchronization overhead by processing commands sequentially on one thread.
questions.explanation: Thread locks incur heavy CPU context switching costs under high QPS.
